correctness.finding: PASS. The stable-offset semigroup identity is exact: writing j+c as a sum of j positive k-th powers is equivalent to writing c as a sum of generators a^k-1, with 1^k padding, so permanent offsets are exactly the positive gaps of S_k=<a^k-1:a>=2>. The gcd of all generators is one, hence S_k is numerical. For q=p^e with e<=k and λ(q)|k, every generator is 0 or -1 modulo q according as p∤a or p|a; an element congruent to -r therefore needs at least r p-divisible-base generators and is at least r(p^k-1), giving precisely r(p^k/q)-1 certified gaps in that residue. Summing yields p^k(q-1)/2-(q-1), and the residue-zero additions under q(q-1)<2^k-1 give the stronger bound. At p=3,k=2 the independently computed semigroup gaps are exactly {1,2,4,5,7,10,13}, so the published universal lower bound 9 is false. The p>=7 inequality and the four explicit p=5 residue-zero gaps repair the prime theorem, and the p=11 corollary follows.
